path_label: Re-run by Hauntlet's demo agent: a scripted agent with no model, reading the generated config through Hauntlet's interpreter. This is not Kiro, and it says nothing about any model.

demo_env_note: The demo agent's environment is empty in an MCP room, as a real MCP client's is (Requirement 8.9), so the credential-egress guard and the SECRETS rule change nothing here: any change comes from steering and the MCP config (disabledTools, and the empty autoApprove, under which every demo-agent MCP call asks and the demo treats an ask as a deny). The demo agent's environment holds this room's dummy keys, as a coding agent's shell would (Requirement 8.9), so a change here attributed to the credential-egress guard or the SECRETS rule depends on assumption A4 (whether Kiro passes its environment to hook commands).

cannot_fix.title: Some client behaviours are out of reach of config.
cannot_fix.text: How a client handles approvals is decided by the client. The most a bundle can do for an MCP server is: leave `autoApprove` empty, recommend not choosing "Always allow" for that server, and disable tools the task does not need.

cannot_fix.title: Steering is advisory.
cannot_fix.text: The model reads it and may still follow an injected instruction. A steering item is never described as enforcing anything.

cannot_fix.title: The sandbox does not cover built-in tools.
cannot_fix.text: By assumption A2, `sandbox.json` does not stop built-in file writes or web fetches.

cannot_fix.title: Hooks gate tool calls, not content.
cannot_fix.text: No documented hook can remove text from a page, file or tool result before the model reads it.

cannot_fix.title: A host allow-list cannot separate same-origin traps.
cannot_fix.text: In the range, task pages and trap canaries share one origin (`/c/<token>`). A host rule that allows the task allows the trap.

cannot_fix.title: A bundle loads only when the workspace is trusted.
cannot_fix.text: In an untrusted IDE or interactive CLI workspace, Kiro does not load steering or MCP config.

assumptions.A1: `autoApprove` and `disabledTools` entry form. Kiro's MCP configuration page calls the entries "tool names"; its MCP security page's example lists `mcp_<server>_<tool>` IDs. This bundle uses plain tool names. Check that they took effect: the disabled tools are absent from Kiro's MCP panel for the server, and other tools still prompt.
assumptions.A2: Built-in web fetch and the sandbox. The sandbox page does not list the built-in web fetch tool as covered, so no sandbox item is credited with blocking it.
assumptions.A3: Loopback under `DEFAULT_BLOCKED`. The docs do not say whether `DEFAULT_BLOCKED` blocks loopback (127.0.0.1). A local range's canary endpoint is on loopback. Unverified.
assumptions.A4: Hook commands inherit Kiro's environment. The hook pages say the command runs in the project root with event JSON on stdin; they do not say which environment variables it gets. The credential-egress guard (and the SECRETS rule's effect in the demo) relies on seeing the agent's environment. Unverified on Kiro.
assumptions.A5: A sandboxed stdio MCP server can still write its own scratch workspace. If, with `mcpSandboxing` on, the range's server cannot write its fact log, the after run is reported as not exercised, never as clean.

demo_notes: sandbox.json does not affect the demo agent: it proposes no shell commands.
The task's own tool calls are not gated in the demo, so the demo cannot show a bundle breaking the task; on a real client the empty autoApprove makes those calls ask too.
